# coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-flash-flash_10-low-threading

<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

Tests **Message Board / Threading** in isolation on `gemini-3-flash-preview` (`low` thinking, 100 steps, compaction at 28K, per-turn step counter) across `flash_10`. Every message receives a monotonic ID (`m1`, `m2`, ...) with explicit reply-to and thread-resolution tracking, an active-threads reminder appended to each turn's observation, and an authoritative thread board pinned across 28K context compactions so open coordination threads are not lost when history is summarized. Compared directly against `coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-flash-flash_10-low-stepcounter` (6/10 overall, 3/10 clean-merge passes).

## Observations

- Agents used the thread mechanics reliably with zero command-parse errors: 22 threads were opened across the 10 pairs and 21 were explicitly resolved (95% resolution rate), cutting total message volume from 167 to 105 and cost from `$4.24` to `$2.95`.
- Despite clean thread bookkeeping, pass rate fell to 2/10 (both clean merges on `dottxt_ai_outlines_task/1655` and `huggingface_datasets_task/6252`, with 4 merge conflicts). On smaller `low`-thinking runs without intent tags or boundary-timed delivery, agents often resolved coordination threads verbally early (`go_chi_task/26`, `pallets_jinja_task/1559`) and submitted faster (906 total steps vs. 1,043 in baseline) without re-verifying their colleague's pushed branch diff before exit.
